name: Planning, zoning and development applications
one_line: J-DEPTH placeholder template for the deciding authority's file on one proposal to change the use or fabric of a specific piece of land, from validation of the received submission through consultation, officer assessment, decision, conditions and appeal. Its distinct default is that the organizing anchor is a PARCEL OF LAND rather than a person, body or instrument: a site address or title-shaped reference plus an application reference binds a content-incoherent packet of scaled drawings, specialist reports, neighbour representations and consultee responses that share nothing but the site. Its privacy default also inverts the schema's: the applicant's submission is destined for a statutory public register while the third-party objection letter is the protected member. It declares no government field rows and no folder dimensions under PR-6.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: these are template-activation signals on a fieldless schema, not licences to write government facts. Every accepted signal must evidence the DECIDING side's custody of a land-use case, not merely a site address, a council name, or the word planning.

an authority-side validation record for a received development submission: a case reference in a stylised application form, a date-received slot, an allocated case officer or team slot, a validation or local-list checklist with met/not-met marks, and a fee-receipt or invalid-application block; the applicant's covering letter and its acknowledgement copy alone do not satisfy the role precondition

a LAND-ANCHORED PACKET: one site address, plot description or title-shaped land reference repeated across members whose contents are mutually unrelated - a scaled drawing sheet, an arboricultural or ecology survey, a heritage or design statement, a drainage strategy, a photograph of a displayed notice - together with one application reference that appears on the receiving stamp or portal header rather than only in the authors' own headers

a scaled drawing sheet whose title block carries a drawing number, a revision letter, a scale expressed as a ratio, a sheet size and a status word, held alongside a validated application reference for the same site; the drawing sheet on its own is a construction or design deliverable and belongs to a neighbour

a consultation apparatus that only a deciding authority operates: a neighbour-notification schedule addressed to properties around the site, a dated site-notice display record, a press-notice instruction, or a statutory-consultee response addressed TO the case officer and citing the application reference in its reply slot

an officer assessment structure: a site-and-surroundings description, a numbered planning-history list for the same land, an assessment against named development-plan policies, a recommendation word, and a numbered schedule of conditions with reasons - held with a delegated-authority or committee-resolution block naming the deciding officer or committee

a determination instrument with a decision word, an application reference, a proposal description quoting the submitted development, a numbered conditions or reasons-for-refusal schedule, and a statutory appeal-rights paragraph, held on the ISSUING authority's side (case-system export path, internal register row, or officer signature block) rather than as a recipient's copy

a condition-discharge sequence: a later submission that names an existing consent reference and a specific numbered condition, plus the authority's assessment and discharge or refusal letter for that numbered condition

an appeal or inquiry record against a determination on the same land: an appeal reference distinct from the application reference, a questionnaire or statement of case, and an inspector's or examiner's decision - the authority appearing as respondent and custodian of the case file

an enforcement record on the same land-use regime: an alleged-breach report, a numbered notice with steps and a compliance period, and a site-visit record naming the land rather than a person's account

an authority case-management export or portal archive whose internal paths repeatedly encode one application reference and one site, and whose members span drawings, reports, representations and correspondence: "A ZIP file named submission.zip may contain a transcript, personal statement, resume, certificate, and form, which is meaningful evidence of a purpose-defined application packet even when the outer archive name is vague."
needs_llm: deciding whether an unlabelled prose document is a design-and-access, heritage, planning or marketing statement written to support a specific land-use proposal, or a generic development brochure about the same site: "It must return unknown where support is insufficient."

deciding whether a site plan showing a boundary on an ordnance base is a planning red-line application plan or a land-ownership title plan, when the title number and the application reference are both absent from the visible text
reading a photographed or OCR'd notice, portal screen or committee slide to judge whether it shows a determination case or an unrelated council service

judging whether a numbered condition named in a later file refers to a planning consent, a building-regulations approval, an environmental permit or a contract clause, when only the bare number is written
identifying that a heterogeneous packet is purpose-coherent for one land-use proposal: "The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent."
distinguishing a policy-making document about where development should go from a determination document about whether this development may happen here
never_alone: a local authority, council, borough, county or planning-department NAME alone - the never-alone rule the schema already carries; a bin-collection letter, a council-tax bill and a library newsletter all carry it

a site address, postcode or property name alone - the tempting false file is `Land Registry title plan - TT123456.pdf`, which carries the address and no application at all; estate-agent particulars and a home-insurance schedule carry it too
a red boundary line drawn on an ordnance-survey base alone - the same title plan trips this, as does a lease plan and a boundary-dispute exhibit

a drawing number, revision letter and ratio scale alone - `Proposed Elevations - 1042-P-104 Rev C - 1_100 @ A1.pdf` is only this row's when a validated application reference for the same site is separately evidenced; otherwise it is a design or construction deliverable

an application-reference-shaped token alone (a year-number-suffix string) - the design forbids a bare number as proof, and grant, licence, permit, invoice and case systems all emit the same shape; planning context terms must accompany it
the word planning alone - a business plan, a financial-planning pack, a wedding-planning folder and a lesson plan all contain it
an .eml from a council-domain sender alone, and a .zip whose name contains a case reference alone - neither shows custody or contents

PUBLICATION ON A PUBLIC REGISTER alone must never lower the packet's privacy posture: a register-published officer report sitting beside an unredacted neighbour objection does not make the objection public
a download session that gathered several site documents in one sitting: "A session should never be treated as proof of topic"
an extension - .pdf, .dwg, .zip - and a folder name alone

neighbour notification schedule, site-notice display record, or press-notice instruction
third-party representation - objection, support, or petition
statutory or internal consultee response
case-officer report, committee report, and committee resolution or delegated decision record
decision notice - grant, grant subject to conditions, refusal, or split decision
numbered conditions schedule and condition-discharge submission, assessment and letter
non-material amendment, minor-material amendment, or variation of a condition
planning obligation, agreement or unilateral undertaking, and its compliance monitoring
enforcement enquiry, breach-of-condition or enforcement notice, and site-visit record
appeal questionnaire, statement of case, inquiry or hearing record, and appeal decision
planning-history extract, register entry, and case-file export or archive manifest
grouping_reasons: one land-anchored determination proceeding, linked by an exact application reference appearing on an authority-side receiving, portal or case-system slot; the SITE is the anchor that outlives the applicant, the agent, the owner and often the authority itself

one received-submission packet whose members are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent for a single proposal - a drawing set, an ecology survey, a heritage statement and a drainage strategy share no topic and belong together only by purpose: "The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent."
one drawing-sheet version family - `1042-P-104 Rev B` and `Rev C` are a version relationship, which is universal and does not confer any government fact on either sheet
one condition-discharge sequence hanging off one numbered condition of one consent, kept distinct from the original submission packet
one appeal bundle, anchored by the appeal reference rather than the application reference, with the underlying case file linked but not merged

one site's planning history across separate applications by different owners over years - a legitimate candidate NEIGHBOURHOOD for review, never an automatic merge, because separate determinations are separate proceedings

a sparse member joins by an accepted anchor without acquiring facts: `Proposed Elevations Rev C.pdf` with no reference in it may sit in the group without an application, site or authority fact being written onto it - the Homework 3 rule
third-party representations group with the case but stay individually protected; a group summary must not enumerate objector names or addresses

no group is a valid outcome for a standalone decision notice, permit copy, or site plan held by a private recipient: "Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group."

template.why: Empty by contract, and this row concedes that its dimensions do NOT differ from the government default - PR-6 leaves the schema fieldless and a template may only name fields its schema declares. The row passes the node test on detection signals and privacy rules instead. The structure the world would want, recorded as prose only: the SITE first, then the determination proceeding on that site, then the document function; the applicant's and the agent's names must not become the organizing dimension, because "It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension." Time is deliberately not first because "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders" - a planning case routinely spans a validation in one year, a decision in the next and a condition discharge two years later. Any later order remains the user's: "The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions."

collides_with.signal: The load-bearing collision, and it is a SIDE collision stated reciprocally with that row's own wording: the authority's copy and the applicant's copy of a decision notice are the same document. Shared fixtures, named identically on both sides: `Decision Notice - 26-01847-FUL - Grant with Conditions.pdf` and `Condition 4 discharge - drainage details.pdf`. The discriminating evidence is which side the holder is on - an issuing or deciding authority's letterhead, internal case file, officer report, validation record and delegated-authority block support this row; an applicant's or agent's submission, its acknowledgement, and the conditions the holder must discharge support that row. The application reference appears on both copies and discriminates nothing. A second discriminator is REGIME: whether the instrument decides the acceptability of a land use or its effect on amenity, design and heritage (this row) or the technical compliance of construction with building regulations through inspection stages and a completion certificate (that row). Where neither role nor regime settles, neither activates: “Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement.”

Stated identically to that row's own declaration against this id, so the seam reads the same from both ends. Existing-site surveys are submitted with planning applications, so the same PDF sits in both worlds. The discriminating evidence: an application reference on an authority-side receiving slot, a validation letter, a statutory consultee response or an officer's report supports this row; the survey deliverable itself, with its instructing client and its measurement methodology, supports that row. The competing fixture is a topographic survey of Mill Lane, which both worlds hold as identical bytes.

Stated identically to that row's own declaration against this id. Fixture: the structural calculation appended to a submission pack. An application reference, a validation letter, a consultee response or an officer's report supports this row; the calculation deliverable itself, with its design-responsibility statement and its cited design codes, supports that row.

Reciprocal to that row's declaration against this id, naming the same fixture: `Environmental Statement - Mill Lane redevelopment - Chapter 8 Air Quality.pdf`. This row owns land-use consent and the material submitted to obtain it; that row owns operating control after an environmental authorisation exists. A planning application reference and a prospective mitigation frame place the chapter here; an environmental permit reference and assessment against an existing numbered condition place it there. A site address and a modelled pollutant table count for neither.

Same authority, same site, same instrument furniture - an application form, a case reference, conditions, an appeal paragraph. Adopting the discriminator that construction_property.building-control already published against both of us: whether the instrument approves BUILDING WORKS or a CHANGE OF LAND USE under a planning regime (this row) or licenses an activity or an occupation of the public realm (that row). Fixture: a scaffold, hoarding, skip or street-works permit for the same Mill Lane site is that row's; the consent that allows the building itself is this row's. An authority name and a site address count for neither.

Fixture: `Viability Appraisal - Mill Lane - residual land value.xlsx`. A residual-value model prepared to decide whether to buy or build is that row; the same model submitted in support of an application, and the authority's independent review of it, is this row. The discriminator is whether the appraisal is addressed to an investment decision or to a determining authority as a submission with a receiving slot. A land value and a build-cost table count for neither.

Reciprocal to the argument that row's sibling already published: neither is a stage of the other. A planning permission routinely exists years before any contractor and often produces no job at all - a refusal, a lapsed consent, or a certificate of lawfulness obtained only to sell - while a job routinely runs under a consent obtained by somebody else. The discriminating evidence is WHICH COUNTERPARTY the document addresses: a contract sum, a programme, an interim valuation and a final account are bilateral commerce with a party who can be negotiated with, and support that row; an application reference, a decision word, a numbered conditions schedule and a statutory site visit are a relationship with a body that is not a party to the contract at all, and support this row.

Appeals, inquiries, judicial-review bundles and planning obligations carry legal furniture - a caption, grounds, a deed, parties, execution blocks. Fixture: `Appeal APP-X1234-W-26-3312345 - Statement of Case and Questionnaire.pdf`. The authority's own case file, questionnaire and consultee schedule support this row; a practitioner's matter file for a client appellant, or a private party's own legal record, supports Legal. The tribunal reference appears on every copy and discriminates nothing. This row must never conclude validity, enforceability, extant status or legal effect of any consent, obligation or notice.

Schema-level, and it is where most real corpora sit: a developer, housebuilder or retailer keeps a complete planning file - the same drawings, the same statements, the same decision notice - as its own operating record. The discriminating evidence is owner role, not content: an evidenced deciding authority receiving, assessing and determining supports this row; a company preparing, submitting, tracking or complying supports business_operations. The word planning is on this row's never_alone list precisely because a corporate strategy or business-planning pack trips it.

A residents' association, amenity society or conservation trust builds a bundle around one application that is nearly identical in membership to the authority's file - drawings downloaded from the portal, its own objection, a petition, meeting notes. Fixture: `Objection - 12 Mill Lane - overlooking and loss of light.pdf`, which the association holds as its own campaign output and this row holds as a received representation with a date-received stamp and a log number. The stamp and the log number are the discriminator; the objection text is identical on both sides.

falls_through_to.when: a standalone decision notice, consent copy, certificate of lawfulness, register extract or site plan held by a private recipient has durable value but no authority-side workflow and no accepted neighbouring group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: a third-party representation, a personal-circumstances submission, a pre-decisional officer assessment, an enforcement or appeal record, or a commercially sensitive viability appraisal lacks a safe accepted group; register publication of the case does not lower this
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a development plan, policy document, planning guidance, appeal digest or published consultation report is held for reading rather than as case work
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: a readable site-related document - an unreferenced drawing sheet, an unlabelled supporting statement, a consultee email without custody evidence - is understood but its side or its case is unresolved
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.when: a case-system export, a password-protected submission archive, a proprietary CAD or GIS binary, or a damaged scan cannot be inspected safely
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

falls_through_to.when: a positively evidenced portal or map screen capture yields no accepted case or neighbouring workflow through OCR
falls_through_to.design_cite: Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.

falls_through_to.when: a site or notice photograph carries no accepted case association and no photo-family relationship
falls_through_to.design_cite: One-Off Images may live under Photos/One-Off Images and hold images with no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association.

sensitivity_why: The class label matches the government schema, but the RULE differs and that difference is one of this row's two grounds for existing. The schema's default protects the submission and named-person case material; here the applicant's submission, the officer's report and the decision are destined for a statutory public register, while the protected residue is a NON-PARTY: the neighbour whose objection letter carries a home address, a description of their own windows, and sometimes a health or safeguarding reason for objecting. Personal-circumstances cases invert it again - a disability-adaptation or a household-need application puts protected material on the applicant's side. Commercially sensitive viability appraisals and unsuccessful pre-application advice add a third protected class. The consequence is a positive rule this row must carry: register publication of a case must never lower the posture of the packet, because “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector” and “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” A group summary for a case must not enumerate objector names or addresses even when every byte is publicly available elsewhere. Site photographs and site-notice photographs may additionally carry GPS metadata for a private home.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: (1) This row's honest mass sits on the APPLICANT side, which the government schema's role precondition excludes and construction_property.building-control already claims; decide whether the row stays authority-side-only, or whether a land-use-consent template should exist on construction_property with this row narrowed to the deciding authority. (2) If PR-6 is lifted, adjudicate centrally whether a LAND anchor - a site or parcel concept distinct from `location` - may exist, since it is the one anchor type no other government child uses and no canonical key covers; and whether it may be destination-eligible given that a site address is a private home address. (3) Decide whether planning enforcement belongs here, with government.permit-licensing, or in a shared enforcement row, since the same notice furniture serves all three. (4) Decide how a public register interacts with P7: the bytes are published, the packet is not, and no handling class exists yet to express that.
